Core output | linking history and examination interpretation, diagnostic basis, treatment plans, prescriptions and medication verification, patient education and self-management guidance, and follow-up and referral records into a traceable care file: reviewable assessment and plan records, not just an impression from one consultation.

20—120 minute safe trial | use a fictional case for one off-site exercise: based on the given chief complaint, signs, and laboratory excerpts, write out three differential considerations, list the history and examinations that must be further verified and one condition requiring referral or consultation, and write out patient education key points including medication verification and follow-up arrangements. Nurse Practitioners (O*NET-SOC 29-1171.00, Nurse Practitioners) diagnose and treat acute, episodic, or chronic illness independently or as part of a healthcare team, and may focus on health promotion and disease prevention; they may order, perform, or interpret diagnostic tests such as laboratory work and imaging, and may prescribe medications within the scope of legal authorization; this occupation in the United States requires a registered nurse with professional graduate education. The work includes: analyzing and interpreting history, symptoms, signs, and examination information to form a diagnosis; developing treatment plans based on scientific evidence, standards of care, and professional guidelines; diagnosing and treating chronic problems (such as hypertension and diabetes) and acute problems (such as infections and injuries); determining medication dosage, route, and frequency according to patient characteristics such as age and sex and monitoring adverse reactions; ordering, performing, or interpreting tests such as complete blood counts, electrocardiograms, and imaging; providing patients with health promotion, risk reduction, and disease prevention information and self-management education; performing primary care procedures such as suturing, splinting, immunizations, specimen collection, and wound debridement; referring or consulting when the condition exceeds the scope of practice or professional competence; maintaining complete and detailed patient care plans and prognosis records; and supervising or coordinating patient care team activities.

entries: Assessment and diagnosis | analyze and interpret patient history, symptoms, signs, and examination information to form a diagnosis, and collaborate with other medical personnel to diagnose or treat complex, unstable, comorbid, or emergency conditions.

Treatment planning and medication | develop treatment plans based on scientific evidence, standards of care, and professional guidelines; determine medication dosage, route, and frequency according to patient characteristics such as age and sex, and prescribe within the scope of legal authorization based on efficacy, safety, and cost; identify and manage adverse drug reactions.

Examinations and procedures | order, perform, or interpret tests such as complete blood counts, electrocardiograms, and imaging; perform primary care procedures such as suturing, splinting, immunizations, specimen collection, and wound debridement; and perform routine or annual physical examinations.

Patient education and follow-up | provide health promotion, risk reduction, and disease prevention information; provide individualized guidance on self-management of acute and chronic illness; counsel on medication regimens, side effects, and interactions; and arrange follow-up to monitor patients or evaluate the effect of care.

Records and compliance | maintain complete and detailed patient care plans and prognosis records; master the state's legal provisions on practice and reimbursement; and maintain departmental policies and procedures such as safety and infection control.

Referral and collaboration | consult or refer to specialists when the condition exceeds the scope of practice or professional competence; provide patients or caregivers with information about medical resources; and supervise or coordinate the activities of patient care and support staff.

paragraphs: The work is mainly done in outpatient clinics, consulting rooms, and inpatient wards: O*NET shows 91% have a regular work schedule, 83% have a lot of decision freedom, 74% make decisions daily, and 57% report that decisions are very important to the results of coworkers or the unit; 52% work more than 40 hours per week.

Responsibility boundary | in the United States, nurse practitioners may diagnose, order tests, and prescribe within their license and state law authorization, and refer when beyond scope; in mainland China, nurses do not hold prescribing authority, diagnostic and treatment decision authority belongs to physicians, and the nursing duty scope is determined by institutional rules and competent department provisions.

The daily closed loop is intake assessment, forming a diagnosis and plan, ordering tests and prescribing, patient education and follow-up arrangements, and records and collaborative referral; the deliverable is a reviewable care record and continuity-of-care arrangement, not a verbal conclusion from a single consultation.

components.definition_block: Nurse Practitioners (O*NET-SOC 29-1171.00, Nurse Practitioners) diagnose and treat acute, episodic, or chronic illness independently or as a member of a healthcare team, and may focus on health promotion and disease prevention; they may order, perform, or interpret diagnostic tests such as laboratory work and imaging, and may prescribe medications within the scope of legal authorization; this occupation in the United States requires a registered nurse with professional graduate education. The work includes analyzing and interpreting history, symptoms, signs, and examination information to form a diagnosis, developing treatment plans based on scientific evidence and standards of care, diagnosing and treating chronic and acute illness, determining medications according to patient characteristics and monitoring adverse reactions, providing patient education and self-management guidance, performing primary care procedures such as suturing, splinting, immunizations, and wound debridement, referring or consulting when beyond the scope of practice, and maintaining complete and detailed patient care plans and prognosis records; the actually executable scope is determined by license, certification, and practice authorization.
